method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the NSW Clinical Excellence Commission Paediatric Sepsis Pathway (form SMR060.399), obtained as a two-page PDF and extracted to markdown. Every source_text fragment was machine-checked verbatim with scripts/verify.py against the extracted text. The age-banded vital sign thresholds (respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure, ACVPU) are printed as tables on the form and did NOT survive extraction; they are recorded as input_unavailable and the guideline states that the RED and YELLOW zones cannot be applied from this file. The extracted reassess RED ZONE list reads 'Lactate < 4 mmol/L (or not improving)' where the recognise list reads 'Lactate >= 4 mmol/L'; this is transcribed as extracted, flagged, and not resolved. Antibiotic agents and doses are deferred by the form to Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic, which is licensed content, cited by reference only and not reproduced.

claims.claim: The pathway is for use in patients from 28 days corrected age to 16 years in any clinical setting to support recognition and management of sepsis, with babies up to 28 days corrected age using the CEC Neonatal Sepsis Pathway and the febrile neutropenia guideline used where relevant
claims.source_text: Use for patients from 28 days corrected age to 16 years in any clinical setting to support recognition and management of sepsis … Babies up to 28 days corrected age use CEC Neonatal Sepsis Pathway … Use febrile neutropenia guideline where relevant

claims.claim: Sepsis is defined as infection with organ dysfunction and is a medical emergency
claims.source_text: Sepsis is infection with organ dysfunction and is a medical emergency

claims.claim: The trigger question is whether the patient has any signs of infection or history or evidence of fever or hypothermia plus any of the listed criteria
claims.source_text: Does the patient have any signs of INFECTION or history / evidence of fever or hypothermia, … PLUS ANY of the following:

claims.claim: The recognition criteria include looking sick or toxic with grunting, rigors, pallor or poor feeding, change in behaviour or decreased level of consciousness, persistent tachycardia, severe unexplained pain, and non-blanching rash
claims.source_text: Looks sick or toxic - grunting, rigors, pallor, poor feeding … Change in behaviour or decreased level of consciousness … Persistent tachycardia … Severe unexplained pain … Non-blanching rash

claims.claim: The recognition criteria also include parental, carer or clinician concern, immunocompromised or complex medical history, re-presentation or worsening with the same illness, being under 3 months of age, central line or invasive device, recent surgery, burn or wound, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
claims.source_text: Parental, carer or clinician concern … Immunocompromised or complex medical history … Re-presentation or worsening with same illness … Under 3 months of age … Central line or invasive device … Recent surgery, burn, wound … Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people

claims.claim: Clinicians should commence an A to G assessment and document a full set of vital sign observations including blood pressure
claims.source_text: Commence A-G assessment and document a full set of vital sign observations including blood pressure

claims.claim: Laboratory features of severe illness or organ dysfunction include acidosis, low platelets, elevated creatinine, elevated CRP or coagulopathy
claims.source_text: Laboratory features of severe illness / organ dysfunction include acidosis, low platelets, elevated creatinine, elevated CRP or coagulopathy

claims.claim: Red zone criteria include a lactate of 4 mmol/L or above, and yellow zone criteria include central capillary refill of 3 seconds or more and a lactate of 2.0 to 3.9 mmol/L
claims.source_text: Any of the following RED ZONE criteria: … Lactate >= 4 mmol/L … Any of the following YELLOW ZONE criteria: … Central capillary refill >= 3 seconds … Lactate 2.0 to 3.9 mmol/L

claims.claim: Yellow zone criteria prompt a clinical review within 30 minutes as per local CERS and consultation with the senior clinician, while red zone criteria prompt a rapid response as per local CERS
claims.source_text: Call for a CLINICAL REVIEW within 30 minutes (as per local CERS) AND consult with the SENIOR CLINICIAN … Call a RAPID RESPONSE (as per local CERS)

claims.claim: The senior clinician decides whether the patient has sepsis, with probable sepsis with or without signs of shock requiring resuscitation and treatment within 60 minutes, possible sepsis with no signs of shock requiring investigation and treatment within 3 hours, and sepsis unlikely requiring consideration of other causes of deterioration and reconsideration of sepsis if the patient deteriorates
claims.source_text: Does the senior clinician consider the patient has sepsis? … PROBABLE SEPSIS (with or without signs of shock) … Treat within 60 minutes … POSSIBLE SEPSIS (no signs of shock) … Investigate … Treat within 3 hours … SEPSIS UNLIKELY … Consider other causes of deterioration … Reconsider sepsis if the patient deteriorates

claims.claim: Actions 1 to 5 must be completed within 60 minutes with ongoing A to G assessment
claims.source_text: Complete actions 1 to 5 within 60 minutes with ongoing A-G assessment

claims.claim: Action 1 is to get help by consulting with a paediatrician, emergency physician, ICU or NETS within 5 minutes
claims.source_text: 1. Get help | Consult with Paediatrician / Emergency Physician / ICU / NETS WITHIN 5 min

claims.claim: Action 2 is to commence monitoring and give oxygen as required to maintain SpO2 at 95 per cent or above
claims.source_text: 2. Commence monitoring | Give oxygen as required to maintain SpO2>=95%

claims.claim: Vascular access should be obtained within 5 minutes, using intraosseous access if no vascular access, with blood culture taken prior to antibiotics using 3 mL in a paediatric bottle or 10 mL in an adult bottle, and all relevant cultures collected where possible
claims.source_text: Obtain vascular access within 5 minutes (intraosseous access if no vascular access) … Take blood culture prior to antibiotics (3mL in paediatric or 10mL in adult bottle) … Where possible collect all relevant cultures

claims.claim: Clinicians should not wait for test results and should commence fluids and antibiotics
claims.source_text: Do not wait for test results: commence fluids and antibiotics

claims.claim: Antibiotics should follow Therapeutic Guidelines Antibiotic, or a local guideline, or the Australian Clinical Practice Guidelines antimicrobial guidelines, with the source of infection documented if known
claims.source_text: Use Therapeutic Guidelines; Antibiotic OR local guideline OR Australian Clinical Practice Guidelines - antimicrobial guidelines … Document source of infection if known

claims.claim: IM ceftriaxone should be given if IV or intraosseous access is not obtained within 15 minutes
claims.source_text: Give IM ceftriaxone if IV or intraosseous access is not obtained within 15 minutes

claims.claim: Fluid resuscitation is 20 mL/kg sodium chloride 0.9 per cent IV or intraosseous as a rapid bolus with assessment of response, and a second 20 mL/kg bolus considered
claims.source_text: Administer 20 mL/kg sodium chloride 0.9% IV or intraosseous rapid bolus … Assess response … Consider giving a second 20 mL/kg sodium chloride 0.9% IV or intraosseous rapid bolus

claims.claim: If the blood glucose level is below 3 mmol/L, 2 mL/kg of glucose 10 per cent should be given
claims.source_text: If BGL < 3 mmol/L give 2 mL/kg glucose 10%

claims.claim: At reassessment the question is whether the patient has any persistent signs of sepsis following 40 mL/kg bolus fluid, with yellow zone criteria including urine output below 1 mL/kg/hr or hypoglycaemia, acidosis, low white cell count or abnormal coagulation
claims.source_text: Does the patient have any persistent signs of sepsis following 40 mL/kg bolus fluid? … Urine output < 1 mL/kg/hr OR hypoglycaemia, acidosis, low white cell count or abnormal coagulation

claims.claim: Where persistent signs are present, advice should be sought immediately from local or regional paediatric experts and Intensive Care or NETS contacted on 1300 36 25 00
claims.source_text: Seek advice immediately from local / regional paediatric experts AND Contact Intensive Care / NETS Tel: 1300 36 25 00

claims.claim: An adrenaline or epinephrine infusion should be prepared as per the NETS Clinical Calculator and can be given via peripheral IV or intraosseous access, and the management plan should be discussed with the family or carers
claims.source_text: Prepare adrenaline (epinephrine) infusion as per the NETS Clinical Calculator - can be given via peripheral IV or intraosseous access … Discuss management plan with the family / carers

claims.claim: The pathway is a form completed with a printed name and signature and carries the phases RECOGNISE and RESPOND AND ESCALATE
claims.source_text: Print Name: | Signature: … RECOGNISE … RESPOND & ESCALATE … PAEDIATRIC SEPSIS PATHWAY … SMR060.399

claims.claim: The reassess red zone list as extracted reads lactate less than 4 mmol/L or not improving, which differs from the recognise list of lactate 4 mmol/L or above
claims.source_text: Lactate < 4 mmol/L (or not improving)
